newsitem.title: BULGARIA: SOCCER-BULGARIA READY TO PLAY WITHOUT STOICHKOV.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BULGARIA READY TO PLAY WITHOUT STOICHKOV.

text.p: Bulgaria are ready to continue their World Cup qualifying campaign against Cyprus next month without volatile striker Hristo Stoichkov.

Stoichkov, who plays for Barcelona, is at odds with Bulgarian Football Union (BFU) chiefs, who axed former national coach Dimitar Penev and dropped his nephew, Lyuboslav Penev, from the team for insulting remarks on local television after Bulgaria's poor showing at Euro 96.

BFU's newly-elected president Petar Stoyanov was quoted by local media last week as saying Stoichkov had promised him by telephone from Barcelona to play in the European group five qualifier against Cyprus on December 15.
But a few days later Stoichkov said in a television interview that he would not get on a plane to Cyprus with BFU chiefs.
"With his statement, Stoichkov broke his promise and closed his door to the national team," head coach Hristo Bonev told Seven Days Sport newspaper in an interview published on Friday.
However, a BFU spokesman said on Friday there was plenty of time before the Cyprus match and "anything might happen by then".
Stoichkov missed Bulgaria's two World Cup qualifiers against Israel and Luxembourg after he vowed to quit the national side unless the BFU chiefs resigned.
Bulgaria lost their opening match in Israel in September but beat Luxembourg last month.
